雖然有保護精神病患者的法律，但偶爾還是會有人沒被照顧到。

NONE: C2 to make a mistake
犯錯誤，疏忽
› a mistake or something that goes wrong
失誤，疏忽

example: These figures don't make sense - have we slipped up somewhere?
這些資料不對——我們哪裡出錯了嗎？

NONE: › a shoe with no way of fastening it to the foot, that can be quickly put on and taken off
無帶（或無扣）便鞋

example: a pair of slip-ons
一雙無帶便鞋

NONE: › a case to protect a book, usually made of cardboard, with one open end
書套
› a cover for a chair or sofa
椅套，沙發套
› a knot that can easily be made tighter or looser by pulling one of its ends
活結，滑結
› a reduction in the rate, amount, or standard of something
減少，降低
› a failure to happen or finish on time
未能按時發生（或完成）

example: The party leader is said to be concerned at the slippage (= loss of popularity) in the recent opinion polls.
據稱，該黨領袖對最近民意調查中支持率的下滑感到憂心忡忡。
the slippage of the book's publication date
這本書出版的推遲

NONE: › a medical condition in which one of the discs (= flat pieces of tissue between the bones) in the back slides out of its usual place, causing pain
椎間盤突出
› a type of soft, comfortable shoe for wearing inside the house
拖鞋

example: a pair of slippers
一雙拖鞋
He put on his bathrobe and slippers.
他穿上了浴袍和拖鞋。

NONE: C1 If something is slippery, it is wet or smooth so that it slides easily or causes something to slide.
濕滑的，容易打滑的
› informal disapproving Someone who is slippery cannot be trusted.
狡猾的，滑頭的

example: a slippery floor
濕滑的地板
The road was wet and slippery.
道路又濕又滑。
He's as slippery as an eel - you can never get a straight answer out of him.
他非常狡猾——你永遠無法從他嘴裡得到直率的回答。
He's a slippery customer (= person), and I've never felt comfortable with him.
他是個狡猾的傢夥，和他在一起我總是感到不舒服。

NONE: › a bad situation or habit that, after it has started, is likely to get very much worse
滑坡效應（指壞情況或惡習一旦開始就很可能變得愈加嚴重）

example: You're on a slippery slope once you start lying about your age!
你一旦開始對你的年齡撒謊，就再也停不住了！

NONE: › A slippy surface causes you to slip easily because it is wet or smooth.
（表面）濕滑的，滑的

example: Careful - I've just polished the floor and it's a bit slippy.
小心——我剛給地板打過蠟，有點滑。

slippery

NONE: › (especially of a piece of work) showing little care, effort, or attention
（尤指工作）馬虎的，不嚴謹的

example: She complained that the carpenter's work had been slipshod.
她抱怨那個木匠的工作太馬虎了。

NONE: › a current of air behind a quickly moving object, such as a car travelling extremely fast or an aircraft
（高速行駛的汽車、飛機後的）逸流，滑流
› a sloping track used to move boats into or out of the water
（船的）下水滑道，船臺
› to make a long, straight, narrow cut in something
撕裂，切開；在…上開狹長裂縫
› a straight, narrow cut or opening in something
裂縫

example: He slit open the envelope with a knife.
他用刀將信封裁開。
She killed herself by slitting her wrists.
她割腕自殺了。
He was found the next day with his throat slit.
第二天有人發現他被割斷了喉嚨。
She was wearing one of those skirts that's slit up the front.
她穿了一條那種前面開衩的裙子。
Make a small slit in each chicken breast and push in a piece of garlic.
在每塊雞胸上切個小口，塞進一瓣蒜。

NONE: › (of bodies) to move easily and quickly across a surface while twisting or curving
（軀體）蜿蜒而行，曲折滑行

example: She watched the snake slither away.
她看著蛇滑走了。

NONE: › a very small, thin piece of something, usually broken off something larger
碎片，薄片

example: a sliver of glass
一塊玻璃碎片
Just a sliver of cake for me, please - I shouldn't really be having any.
只要一小塊蛋糕就好——我真的不該吃的。
